en: Now begins the forty-first chapter: On Specific Combinations for Wealth.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the specific planetary configurations for wealth, by which configuration one born becomes certain to be wealthy. (1)
In the fifth house, which is the domain of Bhṛgu (Venus), being conjoined with Venus,
and with Mars situated in the eleventh house, one becomes a master of abundant wealth.
But when the Moon is in that fifth house, the field of Mercury, conjoined with Mercury, and Mars and Jupiter are in the eleventh house, one becomes a master of great wealth. || 3 ||
And when that fifth solar house is conjoined with the Sun, and the eleventh house is enriched by Saturn, the Moon,
and Jupiter, one becomes a master of abundant wealth.
But in the fifth house, which is the domain of Saturn, when it is conjoined with Saturn,
and when the eleventh house is joined by the Sun and the Moon, one becomes a master of great wealth.
But when that fifth house, the field of the Guru, is conjoined with Jupiter,
and Mercury is situated in the eleventh house, one born [therein] becomes a leader of great wealth.
But in the fifth house, when that is the domain of Mars and is conjoined with Mars,
and Venus is situated in the eleventh house, one becomes a master of abundant wealth.
But in the fifth [house], when that lunar field is conjoined with the Moon and Saturn is situated in the eleventh house, the one born becomes a master of abundant wealth. || 8 ||
If the ascendant is situated in the sign of the Sun (Leo) and is further conjoined with the Sun,
and is both conjoined with and aspected by Mars and Jupiter, the person born will be endowed with wealth.

If the ascendant is situated in the lunar mansion of Candrā (Mṛgaśirā) and is conjoined with the Moon, and is further conjoined with or aspected by Mercury and Jupiter, the person born shall be wealthy. || 10 ||
When the ascendant has gone to the domain of Mars and is conjoined with Mars, and is joined or aspected by Mercury, Venus, and Saturn, a man shall become illustrious. (11)
When the ascendant has entered the field of Mercury and is conjoined with Mercury,
or is conjoined with and aspected by Saturn and Jupiter, the person born shall be endowed with wealth.
When the ascendant is situated in the field of Jupiter and is conjoined with Jupiter, or conjoined with and aspected by Mercury and Mars, a man is born wealthy. || 13 ||
If the ascendant is situated in Bhṛgukṣetra and is conjoined with Venus, and is both conjoined with and aspected by Saturn and Mercury, the person born therein shall be wealthy. (14)
If the ascendant is situated in the sign of Saturn and is conjoined with Saturn, and is further conjoined with or aspected by Mars and Jupiter, the person born will be endowed with wealth. || 15 ||

The two lords of wealth and the two lords of righteousness, or whatever planets are conjoined with them—these too, during their respective periods, are givers of wealth; of this there is no doubt. (16)

Regarding the conjunctions of planets mentioned above, the wise should infer the results by distinguishing between the malefic and benefic divisions and through the discernment of their relative strengths and weaknesses. || 17 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in the Pārijāta yoga, then that man becomes a donor;
indeed, in the Uttama yoga he is a supreme donor, and in the Gopura yoga he is endowed with manliness.
In the Siṃhāsana portion, one becomes honored; in the Pārāvata portion, a hero;
in the Devaloka portion, a presiding officer of an assembly; and in the Brahmaloka portion, he is considered a sage.
In the Airāvata portion, one is contented, and no adverse planetary conjunction occurs.
When Pārijāta is the lord of the daughter, the lore is indeed appropriate to the lineage;
it should be known as "excellent" when it is excellent, and marked by the world [bhuvana] at Gopura.
Likewise, on the lion-throne she should be described as accompanied by her ministers;
and on the pigeon, O best of the twice-born, she is to be known as Brahmavidyā.
When the Lord of the Sun is situated in Devaloka, Karmayoga arises;
Upāsanā occurs in Brahmaloka, and Bhakti occurs in the portion belonging to Arāvat. (22)
When Dharmeśa is situated in Pārijāta, one is a Tīrthaṃkara in this birth;
it should be known that one was also a Tīrthaṃkara in a previous birth when [Dharmeśa] was in Uttamāṃśaka.
In Gaupura, he will be a performer of sacrifices, and in his next birth,
that hero will sit upon the throne, truthful and with senses conquered.
Having renounced all phenomena and taken refuge in the single state of Brahman,
he became supreme and like a swan in this very birth.
Whether he carries a staff or a triple-staff, there is no doubt that he goes to the world of the gods;
by performing the horse sacrifice, he goes to the world of Brahmā, equal to that of Śakra.
O best of the twice-born, on Airāvata, the righteous Dharma himself will become incarnate as Śrī Rāma, born from Kuntī’s son and others, just as [you] were born.

The position of Viṣṇu is a quadrant (kendram), and the position of Lakṣmī is a trine (trikoṇakam). Due to the relationship between their respective lords, the royal yoga (rājayoga) previously mentioned is formed. || 28 ||
If those two are situated in Pārijāta, the king is a protector of the world;
if they are in Uttama, the king is supreme, possessing elephants, horses, chariots, and other such means.
O tiger among kings, one whose feet are worshipped by other monarchs shall become a sovereign at the city gate;
he shall be a universal emperor (cakravartin) on the throne, the protector of the entire earth.
In this yoga were born Hariścandra, Manu, and likewise Uttama; Balir Vaiśvānara was born, as well as other universal emperors (cakravartins). || 31 ||
Likewise, O best of the twice-born, King Yudhiṣṭhira was born in the current age, and Śālivāha and others will likewise appear.
Likewise, Manu and the others are born in the Pārāvata division,
and all the incarnations of Viṣṇu are born in the world of the gods.
In the world of Brahmā, however, Brahmā and others are born as the protectors of the universe;
formerly, Svāyambhuva Manu was born in the portion of Airāvata.
Now begins the chapter on the conjunctions leading to poverty. 42.
O Sage, many yogas that bestow wealth have been heard by me from you;
O Lord, out of compassion, please describe those yogas that result in a birth in poverty.

When the lord of the ascendant is situated in the twelfth house and the lord of the twelfth house has come to the ascendant, joined with or aspected by the lords of the malefics, the man becomes destitute. || 2 ||

When the lord of the ascendant is situated in the sixth house and the lord of the sixth house has come to the ascendant, conjoined with or aspected by the lord of a malefic [house], one becomes destitute of wealth. || 3 ||
If the Ascendant and the Moon are conjoined with Ketu, and the lord of the Ascendant has gone to the eighth house,
being joined with or aspected by a lord of a malefic house, the person born will indeed be destitute.

If the lord of the ascendant is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house and is conjoined with malefic planets, and the lord of the second house is in an enemy sign or its sign of debilitation, even one born of a royal lineage will be destitute. (5)
If the lord of the ascendant is conjoined with Trikesha (Mars), aspected by malefics,
and joined with Saturn or not aspected by benefics, the man will be destitute.
If Mantreśa and Dharmanātha are seen situated respectively in the sixth and the twelfth houses by the lord of the eighth house, the man becomes destitute.
If a malefic planet is situated in the ascendant, and the lords of the tenth and ninth houses are neither present there nor conjoined with or aspected by the lord of the eighth house,
the person born will be destitute.
If the lords of the three houses (the ascendant, the tenth, and the seventh) are situated in the Trika (the third, sixth, and eleventh houses), and the lord of that [Trika] is situated in the Trika,
then the native, joined with or aspected by malefics, will be overcome by suffering and destitute.
If the lord of the ninth house is conjoined with the Moon and is associated with the lord of the eighth house,
or if it is situated in the eighth house, the person born therein will be destitute.

If the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the ninth house from the ascendant are situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses, and are conjoined with or aspected by the lords of the malefic periods (māraka), that man born will be destitute. || 11 ||
Malefics situated in auspicious houses and benefics situated in malefic houses cause a person to be born poor and afflicted by hunger.

Those planets that are devoid of the aspect of Koṇeśa (Saturn) but are conjoined with the lords of the Trika (the Sun, Mars, and Jupiter) are all said to cause loss of wealth during their own periods. || 13 ||

O best of the twice-born, if [malefics] are in the eighth or twelfth house from the Karaka or from the Ascendant, one becomes destitute of wealth due to the aspect of the Karaka, the body (the Ascendant), or the Moon. || 14 ||

If the lord of the Karaka (the Moon) aspects the twelfth house from itself, and the lord of the Ascendant aspects the twelfth house from the Ascendant, then the child will certainly be of a spendthrift nature. || 15 ||
Now I shall describe the configurations of poverty, along with their breakers:
Mars and Saturn situated in the second house are said to cause the destruction of wealth. (16)
Mercury and Jupiter, when aspected [by the lord], bestow great wealth; of this there is no doubt.
However, the Sun, when constantly aspected by Yama (Saturn), brings about poverty in that matter.
Seen by Saturn, he makes one famous and endowed with great wealth; Saturn likewise bestows such results through the aspect of the Sun. (18)
Now begins the chapter on the calculation of the lifespan (Āyurdāya). 43.
O Sage, you have described the two yogas known as Dhana and Adhana;
O high-minded one, please explain the knowledge of the lifespan of men.
Well asked by you, O Brahmin, out of a desire for the welfare of people!
I shall relate the knowledge of lifespan, which is difficult even for the gods to comprehend.
The various classifications of the knowledge of lifespan have been proclaimed in many ways by many [teachers]; taking their essential core, I shall set it forth before you. (3)
Planets bestow longevity according to their positions as exalted, debilitated, and so forth;
constellations and zodiac signs do not do so by virtue of their own respective strengths.
O best of the twice-born, I shall first explain there the duration of life based on the positions of the planets; listen with a one-pointed mind.
In this [calculation], for the planets beginning with the Sun when they are situated in their respective exaltations, the days are respectively nine, one, twenty-five, fifteen, fifteen, and one. (6)
Twenty years are proclaimed as the aggregate of life by nature;
when [the planets] are in their signs of debilitation, half of this should be known, and in between, by proportionate calculation.

In the calculation of one's own purity, the planet [longitude] must be subtracted from the circle of signs (twelve signs) if it is less than six signs; [the remainder] multiplied by its own numerical value and divided by the measure of the signs and so forth yields the years. (8)
When set, a planet shall take half of its own [longitude], except for Venus and Saturn;
when in retrograde motion, except for Mercury and Jupiter, a planet shall take one-third of its own sign.

A malefic planet situated to the left of the expenditure (vyaya) from the ascendant takes away one-half, one-third, one-fourth, one-fifth, one-sixth, or one-seventh part respectively; a benefic planet takes half of that.
When there is one planet among many, that strong planet shall take its own portion;
in this case, the sages have not declared the waning moon to be malefic. (11)

Having multiplied the minutes of the ascendant’s degrees by the respective lifespan of each planet, one should divide [the product] by the minutes of a zodiacal circle; the resulting quotient in years and so forth should be subtracted. (12)
O best of the twice-born, when the Sun, Mars, and Saturn are situated in the ascendant of one's own lifespan, one should subtract half of that [lifespan] if they are aspected by benefics.

Some learned authorities maintain that the years of the ascendant's lifespan are equal to the number of signs of the ascendant, while the months and so forth are derived through proportion from the degrees and other subdivisions. (14)

The period from the ascendant shall be equal to the [relevant] degree; in the interval between them, it is calculated by proportion. When its lord is endowed with strength, the period is equal to the sign; and when the lord of the [sign's] degree is so endowed, it is equal to the degree.
Now, O Brahmin, I shall describe the natural life-spans of the planets:
for the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, the Sun, and Saturn, the years are in their respective order. (16)
One, two, one, and one for the nails; four, five, and fifty indeed for the *kṛti* [periods].
These natural (*nisargaja*) periods are to be known as occurring in sequence from the time of birth. (17)
Now I shall describe the calculation of the lifespan based on degrees for planets together with their ascendants:
a planet bestows years equal in number to its own navāṃśa. (18)

Having multiplied the beginning of the [current] planet by the number of solar days elapsed since the start of the kalpa, and having converted that into revolutions and so forth, the remainder when divided by twelve should be known as the precise years and so on for the lifespan in degrees. (19)
In that case as well, a discerning person should effect a reduction [of the oblations] like a *piṇḍāyu* [oblation].
Furthermore, another specific rule has been declared here by certain wise men. (20)
The calculated lifespan is said to be tripled when a planet is in its exaltation or its own sign;
it is doubled when the planet is in its own navāṃśa, its own dreṣkāṇa, or likewise in its most excellent state.
When a planet has moved into both [houses], the effect is indeed tripled;
when there is loss in both, there is half a loss. Thus is the clear lifespan of men determined. || 22 ||
Having thus calculated for others, one should subtract [the result] from their respective maximum lifespans;
by dividing the maximum lifespan of humans by that [result], their actual lifespan will become clear. (23)
Now, O best of the twice-born, I shall describe the supreme lifespan arising from various species— of the gods and the ṛṣis— which is of infinite number.
A thousand vultures, owls, parrots, crows, and snakes;
and three hundred hawks, monkeys, bears, and frogs.
One hundred and fifty rākṣasas are proclaimed, as well as one hundred and twenty of the naga hosts and elephants. || 26 ||
For thirty-two horses, twenty-five donkeys and camels,
and twenty-four bulls and buffaloes, [the penance lasts] for twenty-four years.
The lifespan of peacocks is twenty years; that of deer and the like is sixteen;
that of swans is nineteen; and that of cuckoos is twelve years. (28)
The maximum lifespan for dogs, pigeons, and cocks is twelve years;
for bubble-born creatures and other egg-laid beings, it is seven years. (29)
O best of the twice-born, regarding these three types that have now been described,
I shall tell you which one among them and at what time should be accepted.

If the lord of the ascendant is endowed with strength and aspected by benefics, the *piṇḍaja* (arithmetic) value should be taken for the Sun, and likewise the *naisargika* (natural) value for the Moon. || 31 ||

O best of the twice-born, when two [planets] have equal strength, the lifespan is declared to be half the sum of their [longitudes]; when three [planets] are involved, it should be known as one-third of their sum. (32)
Now I shall speak of something else as well; listen, O best of the twice-born!
[A person may die] by certain [planets] together with the lords of the ascendant and the eighth house, and likewise by Saturn and the Moon.
The precise longevity is proclaimed from both the *lagna-horā* and the ascendant (*vilagna*).
First, one should consider a single yoga formed by the lords of the ascendant and the eighth house. (34)
O best of the twice-born, one should observe the second conjunction with the Moon and Mars;
one should consider the third conjunction with the ascendant and the horā-ascendant. (35)
If both [planets] are situated in a movable sign (cararāśi), then it is declared to be long;
likewise, even if one is in a fixed sign (sthira) and the other in a dual sign (dvandva), the lifespan is indeed long.
O Brahmin, if one [planet] moves while the other is stationary, that is declared to be the "middle" (madhya) yoga;
likewise, if both are situated in a conjunction (dvandva), it is also the middle lifespan.
O best of the twice-born, if one planet moves alone while another is in a dual sign, or if both are in fixed signs, then the lifespan of the native should be known as short. Thus it is said. (38)
That which is established by three yogas or by two yogas is indeed to be accepted;
in the event of a conflict among the three yogas, [the decision is made] from the ascendant, the hour (horā), and the rising sign (vilagna). || 39 ||
When the Moon is in the ascendant or the seventh house, that [calculation] should then be taken from Saturn and the Moon;
the decrease and increase of the orbit must always be considered by the wise. (40)

In this manner, over three long yugas, there are years equal to the number of moons on fingernails (one hundred and eighty); over two yugas, there are years equal to the directions and the Vasus (one thousand eight); and over one yuga, there are years equal to the tastes and the digits (one hundred and sixty).
In the middle [period], by means of three yogas, the years are recorded as being equal to zero and eight (800);
by two yogas, they are two hundred; and by one yoga, they are measured as four and six (64).
In the case of the three minor [yogas], thirty-two years are obtained here by means of the threefold yoga;
by two yogas, thirty-six; and by one yoga, forty (khābdhi).
Thus, in long and short [periods], there are oceans (4), flavors (6), and fires (3) [of years];
the segments (khaṇḍas) are measured by teeth (32). From these, one should calculate the clear lifespan. || 44 ||
In the case of signs beginning with Aries (Pūrṇarāśi) and ending with Pisces, there is a decrease [in degrees] from the middle point according to proportion.
The sum of the degrees of the planets acting as Yogakārakas is divided by that same number. || 45 ||
The obtained degrees, multiplied by the respective segment as found and divided by thirty, [yield a value];
when this is subtracted from the obtained lifespan along with its years and so forth, the corrected lifespan (prasphuṭa-āyuḥ) shall result. || 46 ||

When Saturn is the cause of yoga, a reduction of the planetary orbits is stated by others, while an increase is also mentioned; however, this does not occur when [Saturn] is situated in its own sign or its exaltation, nor when it is merely conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets. (47)

O Brahmin, when Jupiter is situated in the seventh house from the ascendant and is conjoined with or aspected by only auspicious planets, an increase of one degree occurs in the lifespan previously stated.
If the lifespan were short, from that shortness a middling one arises;
from a middling one a long one arises, and from a long lifespan, one even greater than that. || 49 ||
Thus, the characteristic of the increase of the stages (kakṣyā) occurs through the teacher in the cause of yoga;
by the opposite of this, there would be a decrease of the stages when Saturn [is the cause].
The various divisions of lifespan have now been described by you;
how many kinds are there, when does it become non-lifespan, and when does it become immeasurable lifespan? (51)
The lifespan is proclaimed to be of seven kinds: that of children, that which is subject to yoga, the short, the medium, the long, the divine, and the immeasurable. (52)
In the case of danger from childhood, the years are eight; in the case of danger from planetary conjunctions, twenty;
in the case of lightning, thirty-two; and in the case of minor [dangers], sixty-four, while for moderate [dangers] it is the same as for lightning.
In the divine realm, the lifespan is one thousand years plus twenty;
beyond that, it is immeasurable, attained by people through immeasurable merits.

If the Moon and Jupiter are situated in Cancer and Mercury is placed in a quadrant, while the other planets occupy the third, eleventh, or sixth houses, then there shall be an immeasurable lifespan. (55)

Benefic planets situated in the angles (kendras) and trines, and malefic planets likewise situated in the third, eleventh, and sixth houses, while the eighth house is occupied by a benefic sign—at that time, there shall be divine longevity. (56)
O twice-born one, when Jupiter is in the Gopura division in a quadrant, Venus is in the Pārāvata division,
and Cancer is in a trine as the ascendant, then the lifespan is that of the end of a Yuga.
If Saturn is in the Devaloka Navamsha, Mars in the Paravata Navamsha, and Jupiter in the Simhasana Navamsha at the time of birth, the person born shall be equal to a sage. (58)
For life is increased by good yogas and likewise diminished by bad yogas;
therefore, I shall describe the yogas that produce full, middling, or small results. (59)
When the ascendant is joined by benefic planets and the lord of the ascendant is likewise associated with benefics, or even aspected by Jupiter, then the full lifespan shall be attained. (60)
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in the tenth house and is conjoined with Jupiter and Venus,
or even aspected by them, one should predict a full lifespan.

When three planets are situated in their exaltations and occupy the ascendant, the eighth house, and the tenth house, and when the eighth house is free from malefic planets, one should declare the lifespan to be full.

If three planets situated in the eighth house are in their exaltation, in the signs of their friends, or in their own vargas, and the lord of the ascendant is endowed with strength, then there will be a long life. (63)
If Saturn, the lord of the eighth house, is conjoined with any planet situated in its own sign or its exaltation, one should predict a long life.

If malefic planets are situated in the three *ṣaḍāyas* (the sixth, eighth, and twelfth houses) and benefic planets are placed in the quadrants (*kendras*) and trines (*trikoṇas*), and the lord of the ascendant is endowed with strength, one should predict a long life. || 65 ||

When the sixth, seventh, and eighth houses are joined by benefic planets, and when the three houses [the first, fourth, and seventh] contain malefic planets, one should declare the lifespan to be full.

Even if malefic planets are situated in the sixth and twelfth houses and the lord of the ascendant is placed in a quadrant, and the lord of the eighth house is a friend of the Sun, then indeed the lifespan is full.

O best of the twice-born, even if malefic planets are situated in the houses of longevity and the lord of the tenth house is in its exaltation, a long life should nevertheless be understood to occur. 68.
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in a quadrant from the second house or the ascendant, or is in its own exaltation sign or a trine, one should predict a long life. (69)
If two malefic planets are situated in the angles from the lord of the ascendant—which itself possesses strength—while the ascendant is in a dual-sign house, then there will be a long life. (70)

Whichever planet is stronger between the lords of the ascendant and the eighth house, if that planet is situated in a quadrant (kendram), the longevity will be long; if it is situated in a succedent house (paṇapharam), it will be middling.
If [the lord of the ascendant] is situated in an Apoklima house, a short lifespan is certain;
if the lord of the ascendant is a friend of the Sun, the life is long; if [he is] neutral, it is middling. (72)
One should speak thus of even a very small result when [the planet] is in the eighth house from the lord of the eighth;
one should declare the results in this same manner when that [planet] is situated in a friend's, neutral's, or enemy's sign. (73)
If both the lord of the natal sign and Mars, or both the lord of the eighth house and Saturn, are conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets, they grant a very short lifespan. (74)
If the lord of the ascendant is joined with malefic planets in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house,
and is devoid of auspicious aspects or yogas, one will have a short lifespan or be childless.
When the lord of the fourth house is situated in the fourth house, devoid of auspicious aspects,
weak, and languid, one should predict a very short lifespan.

O best of the twice-born, if the second and twelfth houses are conjoined with malefic planets and devoid of auspicious aspects or yogas, then one's lifespan should be known as very short without any doubt.

When both the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the eighth house are thus situated in malefic houses and are devoid of strength, a short lifespan is to be known by the wise; however, due to a mixed configuration, it is middling.
Now begins the chapter on the divisions of the Mārakas. 44.
O Sage, you have now described the various types of longevity and yogas; out of compassion, please explain the different kinds of death for human beings.
O twice-born one, the third and eighth houses are the two stations of longevity;
likewise, the twelfth and seventh houses are the two houses of death. (2)
Even there, the second [hell] is more powerful than the seventh;
the lords of those two are present there, and sinners who have gone there are joined with them.
Those planets which are malefic are all designated as "Mārakas" (slayers);
during the ripening of their periods (daśās), death occurs for men.
Having first ascertained the measure of the lifespan—whether short, middling, or full—produced by yoga for men in this world, one should then consider the factor that causes death. || 5 ||
Furthermore, in the event of not obtaining these [benefits], there is loss through a connection with the lord of the twelfth house,
or sometimes during the periods of malefic planets, or during the periods of the lord of the eighth house.

Furthermore, the death of purely malefic planets during their respective periods is sometimes considered negligible by the wise, provided that no other planets capable of causing death (māraka) are visible.

Even when there is a connection with its own [sign], the Māraka planet does not cause death during auspicious periods; yet even when there is no such connection, it causes death during malefic periods. || 8 ||
Due to his connection with the seizing of Māra, he becomes the destroyer of evildoers;
he transcends all others—of this there is no doubt. (9)
Now, O twice-born one, I shall also describe the other characteristics of death;
there are three types of applications of lifespan: short, middling, and excellent.
Prior to twenty-two [years], one is short-lived; beyond that, one is of middle lifespan; but prior to sixty-four [years], a long life is declared. (11)
O best of the twice-born, it should be known that the maximum lifespan is beyond one hundred years;
it is impossible for people to know the final twenty-year span of their life. (12)
One should indeed provide protection for children through recitation, fire-offerings, medical treatments, and other means;
for some die due to the faults of their fathers, and others even due to the seizing spirits of their mothers. (13)
Some [deaths] occur due to one's own misfortune and are thus of three kinds; these are the untimely deaths of children.
Beyond that, O best of the twice-born, one should calculate the lifespan of men.
Now I shall further describe another characteristic of death for men:
for one born under a yoga that produces short life, death occurs in childhood. (15)
In this manner, death occurs for one born of a medium-life yoga when the planet is in an enemy sign;
however, for one born of a long-life yoga, death occurs when the planet is in its sign of destruction. || 16 ||

The lords of the twenty-second, third, and fifth [houses], as well as the lord of destruction (the twelfth), the lord of the *vipat* star, the lord of the *pratyari* yoga, and likewise the lord of the house of death; || 17 ||
O twice-born one, the first and last letters [of the name] should be known as the two houses occupied by the Moon;
those two are malefic if they are evil planets, but if they are auspicious, they are said to cause disease. (18)
And during the major period of the sixth lord, death may occur for men;
likewise, death shall occur upon the removal of the lords of the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses. (19)
O Brahmin, if many malefic planets are endowed with strength, then within their respective periods (daśās), there will arise suffering from diseases and other such afflictions.
Among those who have been described as Mārakas, the one that is most powerful is the primary Māraka;
according to its state, one should predict death or suffering. (21)

If Rāhu or Ketu is in the ascendant, the seventh house, the eighth, or the twelfth; or if it is in the seventh house from the lord of the malefics, or conjoined with the lord of the malefics; || 22 ||
He should be known as a bringer of death even during his own major and minor periods;
for one born in Capricorn or Scorpio, Rāhu bestows death. (23)
Rāhu situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from that [ascendant] will cause suffering;
however, if it is joined with or aspected by benefic planets, it is not considered to be a causer of distress. (24)
O best of the twice-born, if the third house from the ascendant is conjoined with a strong Sun,
his death should be known to be caused by the king.
If the third house is conjoined with or aspected by the Moon, death occurs from consumption;
if it is conjoined with Mars, death shall come through wounds, weapons, fire, burns, and the like.
O twice-born one, if the third house is conjoined with or aspected by Saturn and Rāhu,
death from poisoning, or from water or fire-affliction, must be predicted.
O twice-born one, death may occur through falling from a high pit or by means of binding,
if the Moon is conjoined with or aspected by Mandi in the third house.
His death will certainly occur due to worms, leprosy, or similar ailments, if the third house is conjoined with or aspected by Mercury. (29)
O best of the twice-born, his death should be known to occur from fever;
if the third house is conjoined with or aspected by Jupiter, death results from swelling and similar ailments.
If the third house is aspected by a pair of Bhrigus (Venus and Mercury), death occurs due to urinary disease;
if that house is joined by many planets, death results from many diseases. || 31 ||
If the third house is conjoined with benefics, death will occur in an auspicious region;
if conjoined with malefics, death will occur in the land of Kīkaṭa; and if conjoined with mixed planets, death will occur in a mixed locality. || 32 ||

O best of the twice-born, if the third house is conjoined with Jupiter and Venus, death occurs through knowledge; however, if it is conjoined with other planets, death should be known to occur through ignorance.
O twice-born one, if it is situated in a movable sign as the third house, death occurs in a foreign land; if in a fixed sign, at home; and if in a dual-natured sign, on the road.
The wise have declared that the cause [of death] is determined from both the ascendant and the eighth house:
if the Sun is in the eighth, death comes by fire; if the Moon is there, death comes by water.

O best of the twice-born, death should be understood to result from a treatise when Mars is [the lord], from fever when Mercury is, from disease when Jupiter is, from hunger when Venus is, and from thirst when Saturn is.

If the eighth house is joined with a benefic aspect and the lord of the ninth house is conjoined with benefics, then death should be known to occur at a sacred ford (tīrtha); otherwise, death occurs through things called "evil. (37)
Death is to be known by the three parts occupied by fire, water, and earth residing in the body;
herein, the transformation of the corpse occurs through their respective functions of burning, moistening, and drying. (38)
If the *dṛkāṇas* belong to the class of predatory beasts, mockery certainly occurs, like that of a corpse by dogs, jackals, and the like, or by birds such as vultures and crows. (39)
In Cancer, the middle and the last [houses] are [the first two]; in Scorpio, the first and second;
and in Pisces, the last third part—these are proclaimed as the Vyāla group. (40)
O best of the twice-born, when Jupiter is the lord of the third part occupied by the strength of the Sun and Moon, one should know that the person has come from the world of the gods.

A wise person should thus declare [the results] from the time of birth: from the world of the ancestors for Venus and the Moon; from the mortal world for the Sun and Mars; and from hell for Mercury and Saturn.

The Guru, Candra, and Śita; Sūrya and Bhauma; and Jña and Ārki—these, in their respective order, lead one to the worlds of the gods, the moon, the earth, and the netherworld when they occupy the sixth or the eighth house. (43)

Furthermore, O best of the twice-born, if at that time there is no planet present, whichever of the two— the lord of the eighth house or the lord of the third house— is stronger, leads [the soul] to its own world at the end.

O best of the twice-born, it should be understood that according to its position in its own exaltation and so forth, [the results] are superior, middling, or inferior respectively, even in those respective worlds. 45.
O twice-born one of noble vows, I shall describe other varieties of Māraka caused by the zodiac signs and planets in the context of the chapters on Daśās.
Now begins the chapter on the planetary states (Graha-avasthā). || 45 ||
O Sage, regarding the results of the planets that have been declared according to their states (avasthās), what is that state, O best of sages, and how many kinds are there? Please explain this.
O best of the gods, there are various states of the planets; among them, I shall describe those that are essential, beginning with the state of childhood. || 2 ||
In due order, [the states] are child, youth, boy, young man, old man, and likewise dead;
when the planet is in an odd sign, these are determined by six parts, but in an even sign, it should be known as the reverse. (3)
The fruit is one-quarter for a child, half a fruit for a youth, a full fruit for a young adult, a little for an old man, and zero when dead. (4)

The states known as waking, dreaming, and deep sleep correspond respectively to the positions of exaltation and own-sign, to being an equal or a friend, and to being an enemy or in depression; these states yield results according to their names. (5)
O best of the twice-born, the fruit is complete when one is awake, middling when dreaming, and the fruit should be known as void when in deep sleep.
Radiant, healthy, joyful, peaceful, dejected, suffering, distressed, and wicked—such are the other nine states. (7)

A planet situated in its exaltation is "radiant" (dīpta); in its own sign, it is "stationary" (svastha); in the sign of its great friend, it is "joyful" (mudita); in the sign of its friend, it is "peaceful" (śānta); and in its own sign, it is said to be "depressed" (dīna). (8)
One born in the house of an enemy is said to be miserable; if joined with a malefic planet, he is deformed.
One born in the house of a malefic should be known as wicked; if joined with the Sun, he will be prone to anger.
O best of the twice-born, whatever planet occupies whichever house at the time of birth, the corresponding result of that house should be inferred for that planet.
Ashamed, proud, hungry, thirsty, joyful, and agitated—these are proclaimed to be the states of the planets. || 11 ||
A planet situated in the house of its enemy, or conjoined with Rāhu or Ketu, or joined by the Sun, Saturn, and Mars, is called a "shameful" (lajjita) planet. || 12 ||
O best of the twice-born, he who is situated in an exaltation house or even in a trine is declared to be "haughty" (garvita), without any doubt.
If [the Moon] should be in an enemy's house, conjoined with an enemy planet, or aspected by an enemy planet,
it should be known as hungry, just like when it is conjoined with Saturn.
A planet situated in a watery sign (jalarāśi) and aspected by an enemy planet, yet not aspected by benefic planets, is declared to be "thirsty" (tṛṣita). || 15 ||
One who has a friend as its lord, is conjoined with a friend, is aspected by a friend, and is also associated with Jupiter is proclaimed to be "Mudita" (the Joyful). || 16 ||
One should know that [the Moon] to be agitated when it is conjoined with the Sun and all the malefic planets aspect it in every way, or if it is aspected by Mars.
In whatever states the planets reside in every respect—whether hungry or agitated—they destroy the fruits of those states. (18)
In this manner, the wise should understand all things in their proper sequence;
the determination of the results should be stated by means of an investigation into their strength and weakness. (19)
Furthermore, one should declare the mixed result when they are joined with mutual joy;
then, if [the planets] are weak, there is loss, but if they are strong, there is a great result.
The man who stands at the place of work while feeling ashamed, thirsty, hungry, or agitated is a vessel for suffering. (21)
If a planet situated in the fifth house is afflicted, there will be the loss of children for that person;
only one child remains at all times. (22)
O best of the twice-born, it is said that a woman truly dies if she becomes agitated or thirsty on the seventh day of his [absence].

For men who are proud, this [planet] bestows the happiness of new dwellings and gardens, sovereignty, proficiency in the arts, the acquisition of true wealth, and an increase in business; such is its specific fruit in this world. (24)
In the yoga of Muditā, there is a spacious dwelling hall;
there is happiness among women who are the ground for pure garments and ornaments;
there is the dalliance of one's own kin and people, and residence in the palace of a sovereign.
The destruction of the multitude of enemies and the blossoming of intellect and knowledge. || 25 ||

Under the influence of a state of shame, she directed her toward pleasure devoid of passion, toward the destruction of doubt, toward the arrival of the son's news, and toward departure; she had no desire for idle talk of strife, nor any taste for what is auspicious.
Even when agitated, its fruit specifically produces a base-born offspring and a wicked mind;
it causes the loss of wealth, affliction of the feet, and the obstruction of acquiring riches due to the wrath of the king. (27)
Indeed, due to the power of hungry birds, there is a fall into grief, delusion, and the like;
from the distress of one's attendants, there is emaciation through fear of mental anguish;
and for men, there is strife with hostile people and obstruction of wealth.
The cessation of all obstacles occurs through the cessation of the intellect by means of despondency. || 28 ||
In the state of a thirsty bird, amidst union with one's own woman,
there occurs a disorder of disease and an increase in visible activities; from the censure of one's own people comes loss of wealth and emaciation.
There is always suffering caused by the wicked and the loss of honor. || 29 ||
Their reclining and sitting, the revealing of their eyes and hands, their coming and going, and likewise their dwelling in the assembly hall; || 30 ||
I shall describe before you the arrival of food, dancing, desire, curiosity, sleep, and the movements of the planets.
One should fill that [space] with the asterism in which the planet is located;
having further filled it with the degrees, one should assign one's own natal asterism.
The wise man, having always combined the elapsed daṇḍas with the [elapsed] lagna, should divide by twelve;
he should employ the remainder in the calculation. || 33 ||
One should again perform the completion according to the method of the ten-fold cycle of asterisms;
then, one should divide [the total] by twelve, having added the numerical value of the first vowel of the name.
Five should likewise be given for the Sun, and two should be given for the Moon;
two should be combined for Mars, and one should apply three for Mercury.
Five arrows should be offered to Jupiter, and three should be given to Venus;
three should then be given to Saturn, and four should be given to Rahu.
Divided by three, that [number] is further remembered as being of three kinds according to the remaining digits:
*dṛṣṭi* (vision), *ceṣṭā* (action), and *viceṣṭā* (inaction); I shall likewise explain their results.
In the case of aspect, the result should be known as middling; in the case of motion, the result is extensive;
and in the case of lack of motion, the result is very slight—thus do the wise understand the results of aspects.

Having then examined the auspicious and inauspicious aspects of the planets, as well as their strength and weakness, the wise should likewise understand that strength is especially to be known when they are situated in their exaltation signs. (39)
When the hot-rayed sun has entered the sign of Cancer (Śayana), men suffer from various forms of weak digestion, obesity, and the provocation of bile;
there is ulceration in the anus, pain in the region of the chest, and affliction by heat. (40)

If the Sun is situated in the Upaveśana state, the man will be characterized by the wandering burden of poverty, devoted to the science of disputation, indeed hard-hearted, and destitute of wealth. (41)

If the Sun (Divādhinātha) is in the aspect of the eyes, the man will always possess joy, be discerning, helpful to others, endowed with strength and wealth, highly eloquent, and honored by the king's favor. 42.
Possessing a noble mind and abundant wealth, a speaker in assemblies and a performer of much merit,
he is endowed with great strength and a beautiful form when born under the sign of Libra.

When the Sun is on the move, a person indeed becomes a wanderer, garlanded with suffering, perpetually lethargic, and destitute of the wealth of intellect; moreover, he is especially afflicted by fear and prone to anger. (44)

When the Sun is the lord of the day, a person is devoted to the wives of others, devoid of affection for people, takes pleasure in frequent sexual intercourse, is skilled in wickedness, is filthy, possesses evil intellect, and is miserly. (45)
A man who is present in assemblies, intent on benefiting others,
devoted to virtuous goals, filled with jewels, a sun among men, a mine of virtues,
and endowed with a dwelling as vast as the earth and the sky, possesses great strength.
He is affectionate toward his diverse friends, the supreme bearer of a portion of compassion.
When the Sun is in the Āgamana [Dasa], the man is constantly agitated by hosts of enemies, fickle, evil-minded, emaciated, devoid of righteous deeds, and arrogant with pride. (47)
When, at every meal, there is pain in the joints of all the limbs, loss of wealth, loss of strength at every step,
untruthfulness, headache, and likewise eating food in vain;
There was no delight in the night, and the mind wandered onto an evil path. 48.
Always adorned by circles of the learned, the scholar was endowed with faultless eloquence in the art of poetry;
he was ever honored by kings upon the circle of the earth whenever the lord of the lotuses [the moon] arose with a desire for dance. 49.
A person who always maintains joy, who possesses knowledge, who performs sacrifices, and who resides in the palace of a sovereign;
who is fearless toward the enemy of the Lotus-Born (Viṣṇu), whose face is his own, and who delights in the playful discourse of poetic science—[such a one attains] joy in wonder. 50.

When the two lotus-eyes have closed in sleep, appearing red from the weight of slumber, there shall be for the person dwelling in a foreign land separation from his wife, loss of wealth, and the destruction of his prosperity. (51)
If the Moon enters the ascendant at the time of birth, the person will be proud, subject to great cold, lustful, and a destroyer of wealth. (52)
If the Moon is situated in the eighth house, a person becomes afflicted by disease, dull-witted, especially destitute of wealth,
harsh, a doer of improper acts, and a stealer of others' property.
If the Moon is in Netrapāṇi, a man will suffer from a great disease;
he will be a talkative rogue, always devoted to wicked deeds. (54)
When the lord of the full moon (the king) has attained full bloom and his son has been born,
there shall be a blossoming in the world for that sovereign who is a mass of stainless virtues; and a garland of new hopes shall arise, encompassed by the splendor of elephants and horses.
Adorning oneself with women is daily pleasure; going on pilgrimage is [daily] suffering. || 55 ||
When the Moon is in its other [dark] half and is engaged in sinful activity, a man will especially become cruel in his actions;
he will be constantly afflicted by eye diseases and, during the bright fortnight, will be overcome by fear while traveling.
A man born under Vidhātṛ will be proud, afflicted with foot disease, devoted to secret sins, wretched, and devoid of mental contentment. (57)
Generous toward all people, honored by the king of kings, possessing a splendor equal to the Lord of Rati, and the bringer of peace to women—
when that one of lovely form had suddenly entered the assembly, [the moon] grew apprehensive.
He becomes one who knows the joy of the supreme tradition and a connoisseur of virtues. || 58 ||
In the Āgamaka division, a man is foolish yet filled with righteousness; in the Kṛṣṇapakṣa division, he has two wives, is sickly, very wicked, and obstinate.

At birth, the full moon brings happiness to people through food and honor; yet, for those who are not white [the dark fortnight], it spreads nothing but unhappiness regarding wives and sons—indeed, nothing auspicious at all. 50.

When the Moon has entered the desire for dancing and is strong, a man becomes powerful; he is indeed a knower of song and a connoisseur of aesthetic flavor, but if it is in Kṛṣṇa, he becomes a doer of evil.
When the Moon enters the house of curiosity (the seventh house), there arises either kingship or the status of a lord of wealth;
constant proficiency in the arts of love, and extreme skill in the pleasures of courtesans. (62)

When the birth [ascendant] has entered sleep (is obscured) and the Moon is joined by Jupiter, there is greatness; if it is devoid [of strength], there is loss of wealth accumulated by women. In the temple of Śiva, it cries out strangely and loudly. 63.
During the period of Śayana (the Moon in Scorpio), a person may become afflicted with wounds;
they will be beset by much itching and especially by ringworm.
If Mars is situated in the Upaveśana yoga, the man will always be powerful, devoted to sin, a speaker of falsehood, and exceedingly arrogant;
though filled with wealth, he will be devoid of his own duty.
When Mars, the son of the Earth, reaches the second house from the ascendant, men then suffer poverty; however, if it is in another sign, they attain lordship over a city.
If Venus is in the ascendant, there will be light even for one of low status; if it is in the fourth house, there is constant increase in honor for the brother of the lord of the earth.
If it is in the fifth house, there will be separation from son and wife; or, due to Rahu, there may be a terrible fall. (67)

The son of the Earth (Mars) causes constant movement in one's travels day after day, brings fear of a multitude of wounds, quarrels with women, and various fears of skin diseases and itching; he also causes the loss of wealth in many ways. 68.
Upon his arrival, he is endowed with virtues like a garland of jewels;
he wields a formidable sword, slays elephants, destroys enemies, and removes the distress of his attendants on the earth.

If Mars occupies the *tuṅga* (exaltation) sign, the man is skilled in the entire range of martial arts, possesses the banner of righteousness, and is a lord of wealth; if he enters the *sabhā* (the tenth house), he is devoid of learning;
at the end [of his life], he is bereft of children, wife, and friends; and if he is situated in any other position, the opposite is declared.
"Surely this person is one who understands royal assemblies, possesses great wealth, is honorable, and is generous. (70)
When the planet Mars is in the eleventh house (Āgama), people become devoid of righteous deeds and afflicted by disease;
they suffer from severe pain at the base of the ears, possess a timid mind, and associate with the wicked.
If Mars is strong at the time of birth, the man will always be a consumer of sweet foods, a performer of base deeds, and devoid of honor.
When Mars has reached the desire for dance, a mass of wealth comes to living beings from the lord of the earth;
the dwelling place of men shall always be adorned with gold, human gems, and corals at all times. 73.
When Mars is in its period of curiosity (kautuka), people become curious; the populace is filled with friends and sons.
When it is in its exaltation, one is adorned in the houses of kings and honored by those who are mines of virtues and possessors of excellent qualities. || 74 ||
When Mars has entered the state of sleep, a person becomes angry, devoid of intellect and wealth, deceitful, fallen from righteousness, and afflicted by disease. || 75 ||
If Mercury is in the seventh house (the house of the wife), the man will be afflicted by hunger, lame in his limbs, with eyes like those of a *guñjā* berry,
a libertine, and a rogue.

If the son of the Moon (Mercury) is situated in the house of birth or the fourth house, filled with a multitude of virtues, the person will be poor if it is aspected by or joined with malefics; however, if it is associated with benefics, the person will possess wealth and happiness.

When Mercury is in the second house, a person becomes devoid of learning and discrimination, lacking in well-being and contentment, and though possessing handsomeness, he is bereft of the happiness of sons,
home, children, and wife; furthermore, he has daughters.
The subjects are for the sake of the king’s household, and the boon is for the sake of wisdom. || 78 ||

A man born under Mercury is indeed a donor, compassionate, a performer of meritorious deeds, one who has reached the further shore of the ocean of various sciences, full of discernment, and a destroyer of the company of the wicked. (79)
There will be coming and going; while you are traveling, there will be many occurrences in the palace of the lord of the earth.
And that palace is diverse and sufficient for delight with Ramā; know this truly at the time of your birth.
If Jupiter is in its exaltation at the time of birth, people immediately perceive that there will be an abundance of wealth in the assembly hall, a constant increase in merit,
or else equality with the Lord of Wealth (Kubera), kingship, or the status of a minister.
Devotion to the feet of Hari and Hara is characterized by sattva; it is the attainment of liberation. || 81 ||
In the birth [chart] of living beings, when Mercury is in Āgama, there is success in wealth through service to the lowly; moreover, there is a pair of sons, and a daughter who bestows honor. (82)
When Mercury is in the eighth house at the time of birth, there is always loss of wealth for the person due to disputes;
there is fear of kings, emaciation, instability of mind, lack of physical union with a wife, and no happiness from a wife.
When Mercury is situated in the third house, the man is endowed with honor, vehicles, and clusters of coral;
he possesses friends, sons, and prowess, is a scholar in assemblies, and—if the sign is malefic—is devoted to women and is a libertine. (84)
If Mercury is in the seventh house at birth, men will possess flawless knowledge of music;
if it is in the eighth house, they will find pleasure with courtesans; and if it is in a virtuous asterism, their intellect will be endowed with merit and they will attain a good rebirth. || 85 ||

When Mercury is situated in the eighth house, there is constant lack of sleep and its pleasure; a state of continuous illness, mental distress, and physical infirmity; great suffering, disputes with one's own kin, and the loss of wealth and honor. (86)
When the Moon is the lord at the time of birth, even if a person is powerful in bed, he is of diminished reputation;
indeed, such a man has an exceedingly fair body, long jaws, and is greatly possessed by fear of his enemies. (87)
If he reaches Upaveśa while still alive, he will become talkative and filled with great pride;
tormented by kings and the lords of enemy nations, he will be marked by wounds upon his feet, shanks, face, and hands. (88)
When [the planet] reaches Netrapāṇi, one who was honored by the king of gods becomes afflicted by disease and deprived of the glory of excellent wealth;
though fond of song and dance and always lustful, he is fair-complexioned yet possesses a fondness for those of a discolored appearance.

The preceptor of Vāsava has swiftly arrived at the forest bower of the Lord of Vraja, which spreads the bliss of virtues and is the root of stainless happiness; it is a mass of splendor and is ever radiant.
He is the venerable one of the worlds and, for embodied beings, equal to the Lord of Wealth. || 90 ||

When Jupiter has gone to the seventh house, a man becomes daring, always filled with joy by the happiness of his circle of friends, and a wise scholar adorned with various kinds of wealth and jewels. (91)

At the time of his birth, when the people of the noble city arrived, the illusory power of Hari (Harimāyā) truly abandoned her dwelling here, having been completely bound by the Teacher of the Gods (Bṛhaspati). 92.
A speaker equal to the preceptor of the gods, enriched with pure pearls,
suddenly filled in the assembly with the measures of gems and rubies;
abounding in elephants, horses, and chariots, he is worthy of worship by the Lord of the Devas.
In this birth, a human being may be proud of various branches of knowledge. || 93 ||
In the Āgama of Guru, there shall be the happiness of various vehicles, conveyances, and retinues;
there shall be the joy arising from servants, children, wife, and friends; one’s learning shall be irreproachable;
and there shall be constant honor from the lords of the earth, as well as an exceedingly pleasing intellect.
He always delights in the bliss of poetry, his conduct is ever humble, and he possesses self-respect in all circumstances. || 94 ||
For one who possesses devotion toward food, the gods, and the guru, there is always excellent nourishment;
at that time, he does not abandon his abode, which is adorned with horses, elephants, and chariots.
When [the planet] reaches Nṛtyalipsā, the person becomes a king, wealthy, and ever devoted to dharma, worthy of worship by the lords of the gods;
he is an expert in the Tantras, adorned by the wise, a scholar, and indeed a man instantly proficient in the science of grammar. 96.
The wealthy person is always curious and full of wonder;
and within his own lineage, Bhāskara is happy, bearing a portion of grace,
honored by the king of the Nīlimpas, and possessing many sons.
Endowed with great strength, he was a scholar at the palace of the lord of the earth. || 97 ||
When the Guru has fallen asleep, one suffers from folly in all undertakings;
his home is overcome by poverty and devoid of merit. (98)
Even a powerful person may suffer from internal disease, be filled with great wrath toward Śukra, be destitute of wealth, and, when lying on his bed, be addicted to the company of courtesans. (99)

If Uśanas were present at the installation ceremony, adorned with ninefold rows of jewels and golden ornaments, there would be constant happiness and no decline in wealth; moreover, there would be great honor from the king and an upliftment of the mind. (100)

If Venus is situated in the house of the Ascendant as the Netrapāṇi yoga, and the seventh house is the sign of honor (Mānabha), for that person there will certainly be a downfall of wealth; however, if it is in another sign, the residence shall become spacious. || 101 ||
When Venus is in its own house or in an exaltation sign, a person possesses the playful grace of a majestic elephant;
he is equal to a king, renowned for his mastery in the arts of poetry, learning, and music.
If Venus is in the seventh house at birth, his mother does not survive;
there will be mental anguish, separation from people, and fear of enemies. (103)

When the son of Bhṛgu has gone to the Āgamana [sub-period], the person becomes a lord of wealth, possesses a wandering intellect regarding his goals, is constantly energetic, and suffers from diseases of the hands and feet. (104)
Without effort, he suddenly attains great splendor;
indeed, a poet who knows his own merits gains confidence in the assembly of a king.
When that slayer of hosts of enemies has arrived at the court of the Lord of Wealth, [the poet’s pride vanishes].
Or [he may attain] equality, being a donor, a rider of powerful horses, and the best among men. || 105 ||
In the Āgamabhārgava [year], there is an arrival for living beings, yet an extreme loss of the mass of wealth due to lack of gain;
there may also be the death of a son, the downfall of people, fear of disease, and the loss of the enjoyment of loved ones. (106)

When Venus is situated in the second house, one may be afflicted by hunger, oppressed by disease, and tormented by many kinds of intense fears; yet, through a young woman, he becomes very wealthy and adorned with the status of a scholar.

His knowledge of poetry is faultless, his intellect is always charming, and he possesses skill in the multitude of sounds from conchs, lutes, drums, and other instruments for singing; this is his wealth and prosperity when Bhārgava has arrived with the desire to dance. (108)
When Śukra had gone to the hall of curiosities, Indra attained lordship in the assembly and greatness;
likewise, for a man, delightful knowledge and a station in the world abide as long as he remains devoted to the virtuous.
While the poet is constantly devoted to serving others and has fallen into sleep,
the eloquent hero, intent on censuring others, wanders the earth.
Exhausted by hunger and thirst, he rested upon his bed on a Saturday; though afflicted by disease in his early youth, he was thereafter the best among the fortunate. (111)

If the son of Bhānu (the Sun) is situated in the Upaveśana yoga, a man who is proud, afflicted by terrible diseases, suffering from leprosy, and lacking in wealth will indeed be subject to punishment by the king. 112.
With the son of the Sun (Saturn) situated in the tenth house, one is endowed with supreme delight and is joined with wealth;
honored by the king, he is a benefactor to his kin, possessed of many arts, and an author of pure speech.

A man who possesses a wealth of various virtues, who is always adorned with the delight of wisdom, who shines like the sun in his manifestation, who is filled with compassion, and who is a devotee at the feet of Hara; || 114 ||
If Saturn is in the third house, one will be very wealthy, delighted by his sons, a doer of evil, and a plunderer of the enemy's land;
yet he attains the status of a king among scholars at the court of a sovereign.
If Saturn is in the eleventh house, one is joined with the feet of a donkey and deprived of the happiness of children and wife;
with a dejected mind, he wanders constantly upon the earth, seeking refuge among the lonely.
When the son of the Sun (Saturn) enters the assembly, a man of great luster who is full of statesmanship constantly attains joy through a multitude of jewels, gold, and pearls. (117)
When the son of the Lotus-Born (the Moon) enters the asterism Āśleṣā, for men there is the onset of disease;
at that time, the movement of the lord of the earth is exceedingly slow, and his mind is always devoid of the desire to beg.
When the son of the Sun (Saturn) is in conjunction [with the Moon], there is eating, eating accompanied by savory flavors;
yet there is dullness of vision, and the mind is tormented by the heat of delusion. (119)
When Mars is situated in the third house, a man becomes righteous, wealthy, honored by kings, wise, and a great hero on the field of battle. (120)

When the son of the Sun (Saturn) attains the state of curiosity, a man becomes filled with wealth, exceedingly happy, and saturated with the joy of beautiful women; he is endowed with stainless poetic talent. 121.
When the son of the Lord of Day has gone to sleep, the wealthy man is always endowed with excellent qualities;
he is valiant, a slayer of fierce enemies, and skilled in the knowledge of the movements of the beautiful women of the forest.
When Rāhu has entered the state of sleep at the time of one's birth, there is an influx [of wealth];
furthermore, when he is in Taurus, Gemini, Virgo, or Aries, there is an abundance of a heap of riches and grain. (123)
When Rāhu has entered Upaveśana, people are afflicted by skin diseases;
one who is honored in royal assemblies will always be deprived of wealth and happiness. 124.
If the two eyes are situated in the Netrapāṇi [division], one suffers from the affliction of disease;
there is fear of wicked serpents, enemies, and thieves, as well as the loss of wealth. (125)
For men, there shall be a splendid seat in a place of light, auspicious conduct, increase in wealth, and constant elevation of virtues; here, they shall become known to the learned,
attain the office of a sovereign, and their creeper of fame shall spread far and wide.
Possessing the form of a fresh rain-cloud, he attained great eminence from abroad.
And when Rāhu is in the sign of movement (Gamana), a man will possess many descendants;
he shall be wise, wealthy, charitable, and honored by kings. (127)
When Rāhu arrives, a man always becomes angry, devoid of wisdom and wealth, crooked, miserly, and lustful in every way. (128)
When the wise Rāhu, that wretched man, has come into the assembly, he is distinguished by various virtues and endowed with wealth and happiness. (129)
If the arrival of the planet occurs when [the Moon] has gone to the Ceda-gau, then there will be agitation due to fear of enemies along with one's wife;
there will be great talk among people regarding one's kinsmen, a downfall, loss of wealth, deceitfulness, and emaciation.
Through food, one becomes deficient in food; such a person becomes dull-witted, fearful of action, and deprived of the happiness of wife and children. (131)
When Rāhu enters the desire for dancing, there is an increase in great diseases;
men suffer from eye ailments, fear of enemies, and the loss of wealth and merit. (132)
And when Rāhu is in Kautuka, a man becomes deprived of his position;
he is constantly devoted to the wives of others and is a thief of others' wealth. || 133 ||
When Rāhu has entered the state of sleep, a man endowed with a multitude of virtues will possess lovely offspring, be steadfast, proud, and wealthy. (134)
When Ketu has entered Aries, Taurus, Gemini, or Virgo, there shall be an abundance of wealth; in any other sign, there is an increase of disease. (135)
When Ketu enters Upaveśa, there is an increase in skin diseases such as ringworm; furthermore, there is apprehension on all sides from enemies, wind, kings, serpents, and thieves. (136)
When Ketu reaches Netrapāṇi, eye disease arises, as well as fear from wicked serpents and the like, and even from enemy royal families. (137)
When Ketu is in the ascendant, one is wealthy, always righteous, constantly traveling abroad, energetic, virtuous, and a servant of the king. || 138 ||
If Ketu is in the seventh house, one becomes the best among men, possessing many sons and great wealth; he is born wise, virtuous, and generous. || 139 ||
And when Ketu arrives, there is various illness and loss of wealth;
he is a destroyer of teeth, afflicted by great disease, treacherous, and a reviler of others. (140)
When Ketu is in its natural state, one becomes talkative and highly arrogant;
moreover, such a person is miserly, lecherous, and an expert in the deceptive arts.
When Ketu is present in its arrival, it becomes the banner of evil deeds;
one devoted to the talk of kinsmen, wicked, and afflicted by enemies and disease. (142)
But when Ketu is in the second house, people are constantly tormented by hunger;
they are poor, afflicted by disease, and wander the earth.
When Ketu is situated in Lipśāṅga, a man becomes impaired by disease;
he has eyes like bubbles, is difficult to overcome, deceitful, and a bringer of misfortune. (144)
Curious, fickle, and fond of actors, women, and strife, he falls from his station, behaves wickedly, and wanders the earth in poverty. (145)
When Ketu has entered the state of sleep, there is great abundance of wealth, grain, and happiness;
for living beings, time passes in the diversion of various virtues. 146.
O twice-born one, wherever the auspicious planets reside in the signs at the time of birth, the wise man should always declare that person’s knowledge to be virtuous and free from doubt. (147)
If evil resides in any state whatsoever regarding one's food, then there is no need for further deliberation even when total destruction is imminent. (148)
And when a malefic planet is in the house of the wife during sleep, one should declare it auspicious;
however, if it is aspected by malefic planets, it is never auspicious.

If a malefic planet is situated in the house of the querent, whether during sleep or even while lying on the bed, one should then declare good fortune for him; there is no need for further deliberation in this matter. (150)
If a malefic planet is situated in the eighth house, whether during sleep or even while lying on a bed, then his untimely death shall occur, either from the king or from an enemy. (151)
When [the Moon] is conjoined with or aspected by auspicious planets,
then his death occurs, especially at a place such as the Gaṅgā.

When a malefic planet is situated in the house of karma (the tenth house), whether during sleep or even while eating, then there shall be the ripening of karma that bestows various kinds of suffering. || 153 ||
O best of the twice-born, if the Moon is situated in the tenth house in both the Kautuka and Prakāśana [divisions], then at that very time there shall be a Rājayoga, free from all obstacles.
One should discern the auspicious and the inauspicious by considering their relative strength and weakness;
thus should the wise person understand all absences in this sequential manner. 155.
